options.a: An FHA loan is used with a down payment of 3.5%
options.b: A VA loan is used with no down payment at all
options.c: Conventional LTV is high (commonly above 80%)
options.d: Conventional LTV falls to 78% of original value

distractorExplanations.a: FHA loans carry the government's mortgage insurance premium (MIP), not private mortgage insurance.
distractorExplanations.b: VA loans are guaranteed by the VA and do not require PMI even with no down payment; a funding fee applies instead.
distractorExplanations.d: 78% of original value is when borrower-paid PMI terminates under the Homeowners Protection Act, not when it starts.

options.a: May hold unequal shares and typically lack survivorship unless specified
options.b: Must acquire title at the same time and through the same deed
options.c: Hold a right of survivorship so a deceased owner's share passes to the others
options.d: Need consent of all co-owners before selling their own share

distractorExplanations.b: Unity of time and title are joint tenancy requirements; tenants in common may acquire at different times.
distractorExplanations.c: Survivorship is the hallmark of joint tenancy; a tenant in common's share passes to heirs or devisees.
distractorExplanations.d: A tenant in common may sell an undivided share without the other co-owners' consent.

options.a: Both interest and principal so the balance declines over the term
options.b: Interest each month, with the full principal due as a balloon at maturity
options.c: Principal only, with interest added to the balance each month
options.d: Interest and principal in payments that increase each year of the term

distractorExplanations.b: That describes an interest-only or straight term loan with a balloon, not a fully amortizing loan.
distractorExplanations.c: Adding unpaid interest to the balance is negative amortization, the opposite of an amortizing payment.
distractorExplanations.d: Rising payments describe a graduated payment mortgage; a fixed-rate amortizing payment stays level.

options.a: Buy and sell existing mortgages, improving liquidity
options.b: Originate new loans directly to borrowers at closing
options.c: Insure lenders against borrower default on high-LTV loans
options.d: Set the discount rate that member banks pay the Fed

distractorExplanations.b: That describes the primary mortgage market, where lenders originate loans; the secondary market buys loans already made.
distractorExplanations.c: That is the role of private mortgage insurance or FHA insurance, not the secondary market's buying and selling of loans.
distractorExplanations.d: Confuses the secondary market with the Federal Reserve, which sets the discount rate as a monetary-policy tool.

va-real-estate-readiness-check-finance-c.explanation: Entities like Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac (and others) buy existing loans, improving liquidity for originators so they can lend again.

options.a: Upon the death of the remainderman
options.b: Upon the death of the measuring life
options.c: When the life tenant sells the estate
options.d: Upon the death of the original grantor

distractorExplanations.a: Confuses the remainderman with the measuring life; if the remainderman dies first, the remainder passes to his heirs and the life estate continues.
distractorExplanations.c: A life tenant may convey the interest, but the buyer simply holds a life estate pur autre vie that still ends at the original tenant's death.
distractorExplanations.d: Confuses the grantor with the measuring life; the grantor's death does not end an estate measured by the life tenant's life.

va-real-estate-readiness-check-property-.explanation: Life estates are measured by a life; the estate ends when the measuring life dies (or as otherwise defined in the grant), and the remainder or reversion follows.

options.a: A zoning variance granted to the owner for a hardship use
options.b: A deed recorded with a full covenant of warranty from the grantor
options.c: The abstract summary of the chain of title prepared for a buyer
options.d: A claim, encumbrance, or defect that may impair marketability

distractorExplanations.a: Confuses public land-use control with title: a variance governs permitted use and is not a claim against ownership.
distractorExplanations.b: A recorded general warranty deed strengthens the chain of title; it is the opposite of a cloud that casts doubt on it.
distractorExplanations.c: Confuses an abstract of title (a history of recorded documents) with a cloud, which is a defect or claim the abstract may reveal.

options.a: Contract dates and times are critical and late performance may be a breach
options.b: Parties may still perform within a reasonable time after each stated deadline passes
options.c: The closing date is firm, but other contingency deadlines may slip
options.d: The offer expires if the seller does not accept it within 24 hours

distractorExplanations.b: That is the default rule when the clause is absent; time is of the essence makes the stated deadlines strictly enforceable.
distractorExplanations.c: The clause applies to all contract dates, including inspection, financing, and appraisal contingency deadlines.
distractorExplanations.d: Confuses the clause with an offer's expiration term; time is of the essence governs performance deadlines in the contract.

options.a: Obtain the highest price by carrying out every seller instruction, lawful or not
options.b: Owe the buyer customer the same loyalty and confidentiality as the seller
options.c: Guarantee the seller a closed sale at list price within the listing term
options.d: Promote the seller's interests with loyalty, care, and obedience within the law

distractorExplanations.a: Obedience extends only to lawful instructions; a broker must refuse illegal directions such as discriminatory or fraudulent ones.
distractorExplanations.b: Confuses client and customer: a buyer customer is owed honesty and fair dealing, not the fiduciary loyalty owed to the seller client.
distractorExplanations.c: Fiduciary duties concern conduct (loyalty, care, obedience), not guaranteed outcomes; brokers cannot promise a sale or price.

options.a: The seller's reason for selling and lowest acceptable price, even if the seller objects
options.b: The racial or religious makeup of the neighborhood, since it may affect desirability
options.c: Known latent defects or conditions that could significantly affect value or desirability
options.d: Obvious patent defects, while hidden latent defects are left for the buyer's own inspection

distractorExplanations.a: Seller motivation and bottom-line price are confidential client information, not material property facts a buyer must be told.
distractorExplanations.b: Commenting on a neighborhood's race or religion is steering under the Fair Housing Act, not a required material-fact disclosure.
distractorExplanations.d: Reverses the rule: known latent (hidden) defects are exactly what must be disclosed, because a buyer cannot readily discover them.

va-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.explanation: Material property defects and legally required disclosures must be shared, as required by law; confidential motivations may be protected.

options.a: Requiring APR and finance charge disclosures for all consumer credit
options.b: Prohibiting lending discrimination based on race, sex, or marital status
options.c: Requiring lenders to report loan data by census tract to regulators
options.d: Banning certain kickbacks and requiring settlement cost disclosures

distractorExplanations.a: APR and finance-charge disclosure is the Truth in Lending Act (Regulation Z), not RESPA's settlement-services focus.
distractorExplanations.b: That is the Equal Credit Opportunity Act (ECOA); RESPA targets settlement kickbacks and closing-cost disclosure.
distractorExplanations.c: Census-tract loan reporting is the Home Mortgage Disclosure Act (HMDA), which tracks lending patterns, not settlement costs.

va-real-estate-readiness-check-finance-c.explanation: RESPA addresses settlement services, kickbacks, and related disclosures in covered transactions (with TRID integration for many loans).

options.a: The broker's compensation is a fixed percentage of the final sale price
options.b: The broker's compensation is the amount above a seller's net price
options.c: The seller keeps the right to sell on their own without owing a commission
options.d: The broker's flat fee is owed up front even if the property does not sell

distractorExplanations.a: That describes a standard percentage commission listing, which does not create the net listing's incentive to underprice.
distractorExplanations.c: That describes an exclusive agency listing, not a net listing where the broker keeps everything above the seller's net.
distractorExplanations.d: Confuses a net listing with a flat-fee or advance-fee arrangement; a net listing pays the broker only the excess over the net price.

va-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.explanation: Net listings pay the broker the amount above the seller's net price, creating conflict-of-interest concerns: they can incentivize underpricing and are banned or tightly regulated in many places.

options.a: Before or as soon as practicable when the dual/designated relationship arises
options.b: At closing, when the broker's compensation appears on the Closing Disclosure
options.c: Only after an offer is accepted and both parties have signed the contract
options.d: After the inspection period ends, once the buyer is committed to the purchase

distractorExplanations.b: Closing is far too late; informed consent to dual or designated agency must come before the parties rely on it.
distractorExplanations.c: Waiting until after acceptance denies the parties informed consent during negotiations, when the conflict matters most.
distractorExplanations.d: Disclosure tied to a later contract milestone is too late; it is required when the dual relationship first arises.

va-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.explanation: Agency disclosure timing is early—when the dual or designated relationship is created or contemplated, per applicable rules.

options.a: Proceed with dual agency once the buyer consents in writing, since one party's consent suffices
options.b: Not create the dual agency relationship; consider designated agency, referral, or withdrawal
options.c: Act as a dual agent for both parties but keep each side's confidential information private
options.d: Represent the buyer and treat the seller as a customer while keeping the listing

distractorExplanations.a: Dual agency requires informed consent from both clients; the buyer's consent alone cannot override the seller's refusal.
distractorExplanations.c: Keeping confidences does not replace consent; without the seller's agreement the broker may not act as a dual agent.
distractorExplanations.d: The broker cannot downgrade an existing seller client to customer status to sidestep the required dual agency consent.

va-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.explanation: Consent is required for dual agency where the model is used; without it, other compliant paths are needed (designated agency, referral, or withdrawal as appropriate).

options.a: Mixing client trust money with personal or operating funds improperly
options.b: Spending client trust money on the broker's personal or business expenses
options.c: Holding several clients' earnest money deposits in one trust account
options.d: Depositing earnest money later than the deadline set by license law

distractorExplanations.b: Using trust money for the broker's own purposes is conversion, a separate and more serious violation than commingling.
distractorExplanations.c: Pooling multiple clients' funds in one properly maintained trust account is permitted; mixing with broker funds is the problem.
distractorExplanations.d: A late deposit is a separate trust-account violation; commingling is mixing trust money with personal or operating funds.

options.a: The listing broker is owed a commission unless the seller personally finds the buyer during the term
options.b: The listing broker is owed a commission if the property sells during the term, regardless of who finds the buyer
options.c: Whichever broker first produces a ready, willing and able buyer earns the commission, with no exclusivity
options.d: The listing broker is owed a commission only if the firm's own agents find the buyer during the term

distractorExplanations.a: Excusing the commission when the seller finds the buyer describes an exclusive agency listing, not exclusive right-to-sell.
distractorExplanations.c: Paying the first broker to produce a buyer with no exclusivity describes an open listing.
distractorExplanations.d: Limiting the fee to in-house buyers ignores co-op and seller-found buyers; exclusive right-to-sell pays on any sale in the term.

va-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.explanation: Exclusive right-to-sell typically protects the listing broker's commission if a sale occurs during the listing term. The exact protection, including any protection period after expiry, follows the listing agreement.

options.a: Avoid acting as the buyer's advocate and stay within the listing agency role
options.b: Give the buyer a pricing opinion as long as the seller is not told about it
options.c: Share the seller's lowest acceptable price so the buyer can make a fair offer
options.d: Refuse to give the buyer any property facts until the buyer signs an offer

distractorExplanations.b: Advising the buyer on price behind the seller's back breaches the listing agent's loyalty duty to the seller client.
distractorExplanations.c: Disclosing the seller's bottom line breaches the confidentiality owed to the seller; fair treatment of a customer does not require it.
distractorExplanations.d: Customers are still owed honest disclosure of material facts; limited service to a customer does not mean withholding facts.

va-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.explanation: Listing agents represent the seller; advocacy for a buyer requires a proper agency shift/disclosure. If the buyer wants advocacy, buyer agency (or disclosed dual agency where allowed) must be properly created first.

options.a: Did not record the signed contract
options.b: Was induced by fraud or was a minor
options.c: Signed under a mistake about market value
options.d: Later found a better deal elsewhere

distractorExplanations.a: Recording gives notice to third parties; an unrecorded contract is still valid and enforceable between the parties.
distractorExplanations.c: A party's own misjudgment of value is not a ground to avoid a contract; fraud or lack of capacity is.
distractorExplanations.d: Buyer's remorse or a better alternative is not a legal ground to avoid a binding contract.

va-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.explanation: Fraud or lack of capacity can make a contract voidable by the protected party. Whether the contract is voidable depends on the circumstances, and only the protected party may void it.

options.a: An obligation to purchase on stated terms within a period
options.b: A right to purchase on stated terms within a period
options.c: A first chance to match any later offer
options.d: Equitable title to the property from the day it is signed

distractorExplanations.a: The optionor (owner) is bound; the optionee holds a right, not an obligation, to buy.
distractorExplanations.c: Matching a third party's offer describes a right of first refusal, not an option on stated terms.
distractorExplanations.d: Equitable title passes to a buyer under a sales contract; an optionee holds a contract right until exercising the option.

va-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.explanation: An option is a purchased right, not an obligation, to buy on fixed terms for a time. The option is usually given for consideration paid to the owner.

options.a: Exaggerated opinion that a reasonable person would not treat as a factual warranty
options.b: A misstatement of a measurable fact, such as square footage or the age of the roof
options.c: An implied warranty that the home is fit for the use the buyer described to the agent
options.d: A seller's opinion of value that must be backed by a broker price opinion

distractorExplanations.b: Misstating a verifiable fact like square footage is misrepresentation, not puffing.
distractorExplanations.c: An implied warranty is a legal obligation about condition or fitness, not vague sales opinion.
distractorExplanations.d: Puffing needs no supporting valuation; a broker price opinion is a separate valuation product unrelated to sales hype.

options.a: Practicing law whenever they fill in blanks on a standard approved form
options.b: Practicing law if they draft novel legal clauses beyond authorized forms
options.c: Required to have a licensed attorney review each completed form
options.d: Exempt from unauthorized-practice rules if the client signs a waiver

distractorExplanations.a: Filling in blanks on approved forms is generally permitted for licensees; drafting new legal clauses is the problem.
distractorExplanations.c: Attorney review is advisable for unusual terms but is not required for every standard form a licensee completes.
distractorExplanations.d: A client waiver does not authorize a licensee to practice law; unauthorized-practice rules still apply.

options.a: Curtesy
options.b: Survivorship
options.c: Homestead
options.d: Inheritance by heirs

distractorExplanations.a: Curtesy is a husband's historical interest in a deceased wife's estate, not a feature of joint tenancy.
distractorExplanations.c: Homestead protects a residence from certain creditors; it is not the defining feature of joint tenancy.
distractorExplanations.d: Passing a co-owner's share to heirs is what survivorship prevents; that describes tenancy in common.

options.a: Public use/purpose and just compensation
options.b: Public use and the owner's written consent to sell
options.c: Compensation equal to the property's assessed tax value
options.d: A blight finding by the court

distractorExplanations.b: Eminent domain is a forced taking; the owner's consent is not required, only public use and just compensation.
distractorExplanations.c: Just compensation is generally fair market value, not the assessor's value used for property taxes.
distractorExplanations.d: Blight findings relate to redevelopment programs; the constitutional test is public use plus just compensation.

va-real-estate-readiness-check-property-.explanation: Takings require public purpose and just compensation under the Constitution. This is the Fifth Amendment takings framework, applied to the states through the Fourteenth Amendment.

options.a: Permission to deviate from a zoning requirement due to hardship
options.b: Rezoning of an entire district by amending the zoning map
options.c: Continuation of a use that predates the current zoning law
options.d: Approval of a conditional use the ordinance already allows by permit

distractorExplanations.b: Changing the map for a whole district is a rezoning (zoning amendment), not a variance for one parcel.
distractorExplanations.c: A use that existed before the ordinance is a nonconforming (grandfathered) use, not a variance.
distractorExplanations.d: A conditional or special-use permit allows a use the code already contemplates; a variance grants hardship relief from a requirement.

va-real-estate-readiness-check-property-.explanation: Variances grant relief from strict zoning application in hardship cases. Variances are granted by the zoning authority, usually a zoning board of appeals.

options.a: Delivering the deed to the grantee at closing
options.b: Recording the deed in the public land records
options.c: Notarizing the deed before a licensed notary
options.d: Filing the deed with the local tax assessor

distractorExplanations.a: Delivery and acceptance transfer title between the parties but do not give notice to the rest of the world.
distractorExplanations.c: Acknowledgment makes a deed eligible for recording; by itself it does not give constructive notice.
distractorExplanations.d: Assessor records are kept for taxation; constructive notice comes from the recorder's public land records.

options.a: Land bordering flowing water such as a river or stream
options.b: Land bordering a still lake or an ocean shoreline
options.c: Groundwater pumped from a well under the parcel
options.d: Water rights earned by first beneficial use in time

distractorExplanations.b: Lakes and oceans involve littoral rights; riparian rights concern land along flowing water.
distractorExplanations.c: Percolating groundwater is governed by separate groundwater doctrines, not riparian rights.
distractorExplanations.d: First-in-time beneficial use is the prior appropriation doctrine, the western alternative to riparian rights.

options.a: 1% of the purchase price
options.b: 1% of the down payment
options.c: 1% of the loan amount
options.d: A 1% cut in the interest rate

distractorExplanations.a: Points are computed on the loan amount, not the price; with a down payment the two figures differ.
distractorExplanations.b: The down payment is not the base for points; one point equals 1% of the amount borrowed.
distractorExplanations.d: Confuses the cost of a point with its effect; one point typically buys down the rate by a fraction of a percent.

options.a: Requires extra payment if the borrower pays late
options.b: Lets the lender call the loan if the property is sold
options.c: Protects the borrower from rate increases after closing
options.d: Requires extra payment if the borrower pays off early

distractorExplanations.a: A charge for paying late is a late fee under the note; a prepayment penalty applies to paying off early.
distractorExplanations.b: Calling the loan on transfer of the property is a due-on-sale (alienation) clause, not a prepayment penalty.
distractorExplanations.c: Protection from rate changes is a rate lock or fixed-rate feature, unrelated to charges for early payoff.

va-real-estate-readiness-check-finance-c.explanation: Prepayment penalties charge for early payoff when permitted by the loan terms and law. It applies only when the note allows it and the law permits it.

options.a: Is reset by the borrower's credit score at each adjustment
options.b: Can adjust based on the index alone, with no rate caps
options.c: Can adjust based on an index plus margin, subject to caps
options.d: Stays fixed for the loan term unless the borrower refinances

distractorExplanations.a: Credit affects the margin offered at origination; later adjustments follow the index while the margin stays fixed.
distractorExplanations.b: ARMs add a fixed margin to the index and usually carry periodic and lifetime caps.
distractorExplanations.d: A rate fixed for the full term describes a fixed-rate mortgage, not an adjustable-rate mortgage.

options.a: Covered title defects and claims against ownership
options.b: Physical defects found by the buyer's home inspector
options.c: Fire, flood, and wind damage to the structure
options.d: Borrower default on the mortgage note after closing

distractorExplanations.b: Physical condition issues are inspection or home-warranty matters; title insurance covers ownership defects.
distractorExplanations.c: Casualty losses are covered by hazard (homeowner's) and flood insurance, not by title insurance.
distractorExplanations.d: Default risk is covered by mortgage insurance (PMI or FHA MIP), not by an owner's or lender's title policy.

va-real-estate-readiness-check-finance-c.explanation: Owner's/lender's title policies insure against covered title risks, not casualty. Coverage follows the policy terms, schedule of exceptions and exclusions.

options.a: The buyer is credited; it reduces cash needed
options.b: The seller is charged; it reduces the seller's proceeds
options.c: The lender pays the item outside of closing
options.d: The buyer is charged; it increases cash needed

distractorExplanations.a: That describes a credit to the buyer; a debit is a charge that increases the buyer's cash due at closing.
distractorExplanations.b: A debit to the buyer charges the buyer, not the seller; seller debits appear in the seller's column.
distractorExplanations.c: Items paid outside closing (POC) are noted separately; a buyer debit is charged to the buyer at settlement.

va-real-estate-readiness-check-finance-c.explanation: Debits charge a party; buyer debits typically increase funds due at closing. For the seller, a debit reduces sale proceeds.

options.a: Maximum interest rates that may be charged on certain loans
options.b: Maximum loan amounts lenders may offer on certain loans
options.c: Minimum down payments required on residential mortgages
options.d: Disclosure of the annual percentage rate to the borrower before closing

distractorExplanations.b: Loan size caps are conforming or FHA loan limits, not usury laws, which cap interest rates.
distractorExplanations.c: Down payment minimums come from loan program and lender rules, not usury statutes.
distractorExplanations.d: APR disclosure is required by the Truth in Lending Act (Regulation Z); usury laws cap the rate itself.

options.a: Fund construction draws as a builder completes each stage of a new custom home
options.b: Let a seller finance the buyer's purchase by carrying back a second mortgage note
options.c: Finance a short-term gap, often between purchase of a new home and sale of an existing one
options.d: Combine a first mortgage with a second loan so the buyer avoids private mortgage insurance

distractorExplanations.a: Staged draws released as building progresses describe a construction loan, not a bridge loan.
distractorExplanations.b: A seller carryback is purchase-money seller financing, not short-term gap financing between two homes.
distractorExplanations.d: A first plus a second loan to avoid PMI is a piggyback (80-10-10) structure, not a bridge loan.

options.a: According to statutory rules (e.g., client benefit or approved housing-trust programs)
options.b: By crediting the interest to the brokerage operating account as a handling fee
options.c: By paying the interest to the agent whose client made the earnest money deposit
options.d: By adding it to the commission paid to the brokerage at closing

distractorExplanations.b: Moving trust interest into operating funds without written authorization is conversion and commingling.
distractorExplanations.c: Associates have no claim to trust interest; its disposition follows the statute and the parties' written agreement.
distractorExplanations.d: Trust interest is not extra commission; it belongs to whoever the statute or the parties' agreement designates.

va-real-estate-readiness-check-va-licens.explanation: Interest disposition is regulated; personal skimming is forbidden. The state licensing authority's rules and the parties' written agreement govern who receives the interest.

options.a: Allowed if the friend signs the access log
options.b: Improper and a security/agency violation risk
options.c: Allowed if the listing agent later tells the seller
options.d: A minor MLS etiquette issue, not a license matter

distractorExplanations.a: Signing a log does not authorize an unlicensed person to use a licensee's lockbox access; MLS rules bar sharing codes.
distractorExplanations.c: After-the-fact notice is not authorization; the seller and the lockbox rules had to approve access beforehand.
distractorExplanations.d: Unauthorized access to a client's home is a security and agency breach that can lead to license discipline.

options.a: Advocate for whichever client signed the first agency agreement
options.b: Disclose each client's motivation so both can negotiate on equal terms
options.c: Remain neutral on price advocacy and keep confidential client information
options.d: Obtain oral consent from both clients before the offer is written

distractorExplanations.a: A dual agent cannot favor the earlier client; both clients are owed neutrality on price and terms.
distractorExplanations.b: Motivation and bottom-line price are confidential; sharing them breaches duties to both clients.
distractorExplanations.d: Virginia requires written, informed consent to dual representation; oral consent does not satisfy the disclosure rule.

va-real-estate-readiness-check-va-licens.explanation: Dual agents cannot favor one client and must protect confidential info within the rules. Confidential information must be protected as required by the dual agency disclosure.

options.a: Discipline of the seller only, not the agent
options.b: License discipline and civil claims
options.c: No liability if the sale is made as is
options.d: A fine paid from the recovery fund

distractorExplanations.a: Licensees who knowingly fail to disclose material adverse facts face their own license discipline and civil liability.
distractorExplanations.c: An as-is clause does not shield a licensee from discipline for concealing a known material adverse fact.
distractorExplanations.d: Recovery funds compensate injured consumers after a judgment; they do not pay a licensee's disciplinary fines.

options.a: Perform licensed activities only within their own license authority
options.b: Negotiate offers for the associate while licensed with a different brokerage
options.c: Be paid commission directly by the associate instead of through the broker
options.d: Sign listing agreements in the associate's name

distractorExplanations.b: A licensee may act only for the brokerage holding their license; working another firm's deals violates affiliation rules.
distractorExplanations.c: Compensation for licensed activity must flow through the employing broker, not directly from another agent.
distractorExplanations.d: Listings are brokerage contracts; an assistant cannot sign as, or for, another licensee without authority.

va-real-estate-readiness-check-va-licens.explanation: Licensed assistants still must stay within license and supervision rules. They must also follow brokerage affiliation and supervision rules.

options.a: Mixing client trust money with personal or operating funds improperly
options.b: Using trust money to pay a client's bills without written authority
options.c: Holding funds for several clients in one pooled trust account
options.d: Depositing earnest money after the required deposit deadline

distractorExplanations.b: Spending client funds without authority is conversion; commingling is mixing client and broker funds.
distractorExplanations.c: One trust account for several clients with separate ledgers is allowed; mixing in broker money is commingling.
distractorExplanations.d: A late deposit is a separate timing violation; commingling is mixing client funds with personal or operating funds.

options.a: Deposited into the brokerage operating account until the contract closes
options.b: Held uncashed in the transaction file until closing to avoid any refund disputes
options.c: Deposited into a properly designated trust/escrow account within required timelines
options.d: Deposited into the listing agent's own escrow account for that client

distractorExplanations.a: Placing client funds in the operating account is commingling, even if the broker tracks them separately.
distractorExplanations.b: Funds must be deposited within the required time; holding the check until closing breaks that timeline.
distractorExplanations.d: Trust accounts are maintained by the broker or firm; individual associates do not hold their own escrow accounts.

options.a: Follow authorized escrow dispute procedures
options.b: Release it to the seller because the buyer defaulted
options.c: Return it to the buyer since the deal did not close
options.d: Split it evenly between the parties

distractorExplanations.b: The broker cannot decide who defaulted; disputed funds stay in escrow until a release, court order or rule-based procedure.
distractorExplanations.c: A failed closing does not by itself entitle the buyer to the deposit; disputed funds need agreement or legal resolution.
distractorExplanations.d: Splitting disputed funds without both parties' written agreement is still a unilateral disbursement.

va-real-estate-readiness-check-va-licens.explanation: Escrow disputes require contractual and regulatory procedures (interpleader, releases, etc.). The broker must not unilaterally award the funds to either party.

options.a: Acceptable if the licensee states it in writing in the offer
options.b: Acceptable puffing because future value is an opinion
options.c: Allowed when the brokerage carries errors and omissions insurance
options.d: Generally improper/misleading and can be a license law violation

distractorExplanations.a: Putting a guaranteed profit in writing does not cure the misrepresentation; it simply documents it.
distractorExplanations.b: Puffing is vague praise; a direct promise of a specific future profit is a misrepresentation, not puffing.
distractorExplanations.c: E&O coverage does not make a deceptive guarantee lawful and often excludes intentional misrepresentation.
